name: native-lib-signatures
notes: Vendor-agnostic ELF/.so fingerprinting for Android and Linux native libraries. Signatures are additive hints, never hard conclusions: a hit contributes confidence, the caller aggregates. Extraction uses backslash-free after/until slicing so the file stays regex-free and safe to hand-edit.

match_fields.any_soname: matches DT_SONAME or the on-disk file name, case-insensitive substring
match_fields.any_needed: matches any DT_NEEDED entry, case-insensitive substring
match_fields.any_symbols: matches any dynamic symbol name, case-insensitive substring
match_fields.any_strings: matches any extracted ASCII string, case-insensitive substring
match_fields.min_hits: how many distinct any_* items must match before the signature fires (default 1)
match_fields.extract: list of {field, after, until} slices pulled from the first matching string

signatures.label: Flutter / Dart AOT
signatures.notes: libapp.so is the AOT snapshot of app Dart code; package: strings reveal the dependency list even when stripped.

signatures.label: Supercell Titan engine
signatures.notes: Shared across all Supercell titles; the concrete game is identified by endpoint hosts, not by this signature.

signatures.label: Frida core / frida-gum embedded
signatures.notes: Frida shipped INSIDE a production app is a strong repack/mod indicator, not an anti-cheat signal. Distinguish from an app merely detecting Frida (see the detection-string signature).

signatures.label: Anti-instrumentation detection strings
signatures.notes: App is looking FOR instrumentation. Candidate bypass point rather than evidence of tampering.

signatures.label: Inline hooking engine
signatures.notes: Also fires on legitimate APM/crash SDKs. Weigh together with mod_loader and private_server hits.

signatures.label: UPX packed ELF
any_strings: This file is packed with the UPX

signatures.label: Chinese commercial packer family
signatures.notes: Covers Bangcle/SecNeo, Qihoo Jiagu, Tencent Legu, Alibaba, Baidu and NetEase packers in one rule.

signatures.label: Signed-script / user-mod loader
signatures.notes: A library that fetches and executes signed scripts plus user mods at runtime. Generic across modding frameworks.

signatures.label: Rebranded JNI namespace on a vendor library
signatures.notes: Structural rule: fires when exported Java_<pkg> prefixes disagree with the vendor package implied by internal C++ symbols or sibling libraries. Implemented as a cross-check, see ELF_JNI_PACKAGE_MISMATCH.

signatures.label: Third-party server endpoint alongside vendor endpoints
signatures.notes: Structural rule: collect registrable domains from URL strings, cluster them, and flag non-vendor hosts that sit next to first-party hosts. Keeps working for any private-server family, no allowlist of specific domains required.

structural_heuristics.label: Section header table stripped or truncated
structural_heuristics.rule: section_count <= 5 while PT_DYNAMIC is present and readable
structural_heuristics.notes: Segments still load, but nm/objdump lose .dynsym so symbol-level tooling goes blind. Typical of relinked or post-processed binaries.

structural_heuristics.label: No readable dynamic symbols on a JNI library
structural_heuristics.rule: dynamic_symbol_count == 0 and library is referenced by System.loadLibrary or another DT_NEEDED

structural_heuristics.label: Exported JNI package differs from internal vendor identity
structural_heuristics.notes: Catches vendor SDKs re-namespaced by a repacker while the original C++ classes stay intact.

structural_heuristics.label: DT_SONAME does not match the on-disk file name
structural_heuristics.notes: Often carries a real version/build stamp that the renamed file hides.

structural_heuristics.label: Custom symbol version namespace
structural_heuristics.rule: verdef contains a namespace that is not GLIBC / LIBC / GCC / CXXABI
structural_heuristics.notes: Gives a free version string for in-house libraries.

structural_heuristics.label: Multiple distinct compiler version stamps in one object
structural_heuristics.notes: Normal for large vendored builds, but combined with mod_loader hits it suggests object files from different eras were relinked together.

structural_heuristics.label: Writable and executable PT_LOAD segment
structural_heuristics.rule: any PT_LOAD has flags W and X

structural_heuristics.label: No NT_GNU_BUILD_ID note
structural_heuristics.notes: Blocks symbol-server correlation and build-to-build diffing.

structural_heuristics.label: Debug info shipped in a release library
structural_heuristics.notes: Inverse finding: makes reversing far easier and inflates the artifact.

structural_heuristics.label: Endpoint strings in plaintext where the reference build hides them
structural_heuristics.rule: url_string_count(sample) greatly exceeds url_string_count(reference build of same soname)
structural_heuristics.notes: Requires a reference build. Indicates the string-obfuscation layer was removed or resolved during repacking.
